vo.text:
Most software has no API. No endpoint, no schema, no docs.
Just pixels, and a cursor.

Here is the whole mechanism. A screenshot goes in. One action comes out.
Then the screenshot is taken again.

The computer is declared as a single tool. Width, height, display number.
Three integers, and that is the entire interface.

The model gets what your hands get. Click, type, press keys, scroll, drag, wait.
There is no privileged access underneath.

Watch one step. The model emits a tool use block. Your code performs it.
You return the new screenshot.

Now find the part Anthropic runs. It is not on this diagram.
The model names the action. YOUR process moves the mouse.

Coordinates are where this breaks. Resize a screenshot and you must map the click back.
Skip that, and every click lands beside the button.

Hold the display at one thousand and twenty four by seven six eight.
Each screenshot costs about a thousand tokens. Forty steps is forty thousand.

The loop is strictly serial. Model, action, screenshot, again.
Prefer keyboard shortcuts. One keystroke replaces three clicks.

Separate two failures. A wrong click appears in the next screenshot and gets corrected.
State that never rendered is simply invisible.

Treat the screen as untrusted input. A web page can carry instructions.
Sandbox it. Withhold real credentials. Confirm anything irreversible.

Be honest about the ceiling. Screenshot-only OSWorld at launch: fourteen point nine percent.
A person scores about seventy two.

So use the judgement. If a thing has an API, call the API.
Drive the screen only when there is nothing else to drive.
